At Unzer, we are driven by the belief that customers should enjoy a seamless shopping experience, no matter where they choose to shop. We are a team of over 700 experts of 55 different nationalities, dedicated to creating a state-of-the-art unified commerce platform. Our goal is to enable businesses to delight their customers with a seamless payment experience.  
 
Whether you're a tech enthusiast, payment expert, or a dedicated support professional, we are looking for individuals who are passionate about making a difference.  
 
Our offices: We are based across Austria, Denmark, Germany and Luxembourg, with a HQ in Berlin.
 
ABOUT THE TEAM

Help us connect Microsoft Dynamics 365 with our wider technology platform. As part of a cross-functional team, you will work with product managers, business stakeholders and engineers to turn business needs into reliable software. Your work will combine Dynamics 365 and Power Platform development with Azure services, secure APIs and event-driven integrations, taking solutions from design through deployment and operation. .

 


What your work will look like:

  • Design, develop, and maintain Dynamics 365 CRM solutions on Dataverse, including data models, plug-ins, custom APIs, model-driven Power Apps, and Power Automate flows. Choose configuration or custom code according to maintainability, performance, and business needs. 

  • Build Azure applications and integration services using C# and .NET, with services such as Azure Functions, App Service, and API Management to connect Dynamics 365 with the wider platform. 

  • Develop and consume REST APIs, Dataverse Web API and OData endpoints, and GraphQL APIs. Define clear contracts, validation, versioning, and error handling with the teams that own connected systems. 

  • Connect Dynamics 365 and Azure services to Apache Kafka through integration services and event producers and consumers. Design for retries, duplicate messages, schema evolution and reliable data synchronisation. 

  • Implement secure service-to-service access using OAuth 2.0 and Microsoft Entra ID, including app registrations, permissions and managed identities where appropriate. Protect credentials and secrets with Azure Key Vault. 

  • Build and improve CI/CD for Dynamics 365, Power Platform and Azure applications. Use Git and Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions to automate builds, tests and deployments, including solution packaging, managed solutions, environment variables and connection references. 

  • Own quality and operability through automated unit, integration and API contract tests, code reviews, monitoring and troubleshooting: document technical decisions and support releases and production incidents. 

  • Work closely with business and engineering colleagues to clarify requirements, agree acceptance criteria and deliver usable solutions in small increments. 


What you need to be successful in this role:

  • Professional software engineering experience, including hands-on delivery of Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM and Dataverse solutions in production. 

  • Strong C# and .NET skills, plus JavaScript or TypeScript for Dynamics 365 customisation. Practical experience with Power Apps, Power Automate, plug-ins, Dataverse data modelling and security roles. 

  • Experience developing and operating applications on Azure, with an understanding of cloud security, configuration, logging, monitoring and application performance. 

  • Practical experience with REST, GraphQL and OAuth 2.0, and the ability to design, implement and troubleshoot integrations across system boundaries. 

  • Experience with Apache Kafka and event-driven integration, including producers and consumers, consumer groups, delivery semantics and idempotent processing. 

  • Hands-on experience with Git, automated testing, and CI/CD, particularly application lifecycle management for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform, and deploying Azure applications. 

  • Sound judgement about software architecture, data consistency and maintainability. You can explain technical trade-offs clearly and collaborate across engineering and business functions. 

  • A degree in computer science, business informatics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 

    Nice to have :

    • AI-assisted development using tools such as GitHub Copilot or coding agents to support implementation, test creation, debugging, and documentation. You review generated code critically and protect confidential data when using these tools. 

    • Infrastructure as code with Bicep or Terraform, custom Power Apps components using PCF, or integration with Microsoft 365 services through Microsoft Graph.

data.title: Management Consultant - Senior Consultant - Germany
data.description:
At Efficio, we're not just a consulting firm; we're a team of dedicated experts committed to transforming procurement and supply chain functions. Our mission is to drive sustainable, measurable value for our clients through innovative solutions and deep industry insights. Join us and be part of a dynamic environment where your skills and ideas make a real impact.
 
Efficio is the world’s largest specialist procurement and supply chain consultancy, with offices across Europe, North America, and the Middle East. We’re a diverse team of over 1,000 individuals, representing more than 60 different nationalities and speaking 40+ languages – and we’re continuing to grow rapidly!
We are recruiting for our Dusseldorf Office where you'll be joining a growing team of over 50 people.
 
Consultants based in Dusseldorf will support clients in Germany and across Europe with opportunity to travel globally. Our consultants provide flexible support to clients whether it is a rapid assessment, short term savings realisation or embedding in a long-term partnership to deliver lasting and measurable value to clients.

As a Senior Consultant (SC), you will have complete ownership of complex workstreams or several smaller workstreams and be supported by junior resources. You should be deemed as a subject matter expert (SME) both internally and by clients and you will be responsible for the following:
  • Managing complex workstreams or multiple smaller workstreams. Often supported by junior resources
  • Managing more junior consultants on projects, making sure Efficio methodologies and processes are followed
  • Driving complex analysis where data is hard to access and using expertise to creatively develop conclusions and recommended solutions
  • Playing a role in advising clients and designing solutions that address complex needs, achieve sustainable results, and demonstrate real impact
  • Effectively managing and owning the relationship with senior stakeholders
  • Planning and preparing documentation for own workstream
  • Taking part in the recruitment process of potential junior consultants
    • Our collaborative and inclusive culture is what makes us stand out. At Efficio, colleagues with diverse backgrounds, ideas, and viewpoints come together to identify innovative solutions for our clients - and so we're looking for our new team members to bring strong communication, empathy, and relationship-building skills to maintain this culture as we grow.
     
    We encourage our teams to proactively innovate and challenge the status-quo, backed by strong analytical thinking and creative problem-solving abilities alongside comfortable proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint. We're looking for team members who enjoy and have experience of digging into complex challenges at a leading management consultancy or in a relevant industry position.
     
    Strong opportunities for career growth are an important part of our offering; as such, we love seeing ambition and a proactive approach to shaping your career to your goals and interests.
     
    To meet client needs, we look for flexibility to travel; you can give us a heads-up on your preferences when applying.
     
    We'd love to hear about any additional skills or experiences you bring to the table. We're particularly interested in:
    • Fluency in German and English
    • Management consulting experience within a leading consultancy, ideally within procurement and/or supply chain
    • Experience (or an interest) in strategic sourcing, procurement transformation, supply chain, operations, infrastructure, or capital projects
    • Proven track record of working closely with senior client stakeholders
    • Deep analytical skills and problem-solving skills, with the ability to isolate key issues and draw sound conclusions
    • Strong grasp of detail and a 'hands-on' approach
    • Excellent interpersonal and leadership skills
    • Ability to confidently improve existing ways of working, recognize opportunities and identify innovative solutions that add real value to clients

  • Du behältst auch bei vielen parallelen Aufträgen, kurzfristigen Änderungen und unterschiedlichen Ansprechpartnern den Überblick.

  • Du erkennst frühzeitig, wenn etwas nicht rundläuft, findest pragmatische Lösungen und packst bei Bedarf selbst mit an.

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere digitalen Systeme, Auftragsdaten und Dokumentationen stets aktuell und ordentlich gepflegt sind.

  • Du bist eine zentrale Ansprechperson für unsere Kunden – insbesondere am Telefon.

  • Du beantwortest Anfragen, berätst zu unseren Dienstleistungen, koordinierst Termine und findest Lösungen für individuelle Anliegen.

  • Du kommunizierst freundlich, offen und professionell und sorgst dafür, dass sich unsere Kunden jederzeit gut betreut fühlen.

  • Du begleitest Interessenten und Neukunden vom ersten Kontakt bis zur Buchung.

  • Du greifst lieber einmal mehr zum Hörer, als Fragen oder Unklarheiten offen zu lassen

Prozesse & Optimierung

  • Du erkennst Schwachstellen, hinterfragst Abläufe und entwickelst gemeinsam mit uns sinnvolle Verbesserungen.

  • Du nutzt digitale Tools und Automatisierungen, um Aufgaben effizienter und übersichtlicher zu gestalten.

data.description:

Swarm Aero builds Group 5 autonomous aircraft and Legion, our command and control platform for coordinating UAV swarms. We're backed by Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue, and our software is already running on real programs and real hardware. Legion is the layer operators actually touch, and it needs to ship fast, run reliably, and deploy anywhere our customers need it.

You'll be a core member of the team that builds and runs the infrastructure behind Legion. Working alongside our DevSecOps lead, you'll own day-to-day pipelines, environments, and deployments so our engineers can move quickly without breaking the things operators depend on. What we're looking for

  • 4 to 8 years in DevOps, platform, SRE, or infrastructure engineering

  • Scripting in Python, Go, or Bash

  • Active Secret clearance or higher strongly preferred; must be able to obtain and maintain a US security clearance

  • Willingness to travel to customer and test sites

Nice to have

  • Experience deploying to air-gapped, disconnected, or edge environments

  • Background in defense tech, government programs, or regulated environments

  • Experience supporting real-time or mission-critical systems

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

data.title: Team Lead Software Production Support (m/f/d)
data.description:
At Quantum Systems, we are redefining the boundaries of autonomous drone technology. We develop and deploy some of the world’s most advanced UAVs, combining highly integrated hardware, embedded software, sensors, compute platforms, and production processes into reliable systems for demanding real-world missions.​

As part of our Software Production Support Team, you will work at the intersection of serial UAV production, embedded software, firmware deployment, production diagnostics, automation, and traceability. You will help ensure that every drone leaving production is equipped with the correct software, firmware, configuration, and documentation needed for safe and reliable operation.​

Between hands-on troubleshooting on the production floor, flashing microcontrollers and compute modules, analyzing system behavior, improving diagnostic workflows, developing production tools, and refining digital work instructions, you will play a key role in turning advanced UAV technology into stable, scalable, and efficient serial production



What is your Day to Day Mission:

  • Leading and developing the Software Production Support team​.

  • Prioritizing urgent production support topics and long-term improvement activities​.

  • Identifying bottlenecks, recurring issues, and process weaknesses in serial production​.

  • Defining robust processes for microcontroller flashing, NVIDIA Orin installation, firmware updates, diagnostics, and recovery workflows​.

  • Driving automation and standardization of software-related production steps​.

  • Ensuring that production tools are reliable, versioned, documented, and maintainable​.

  • Defining requirements for production traceability and digital paper trail documentation​.

  • Coordinating software-related production escalations with Engineering, Quality, and Industrialization​.

  • Monitoring KPIs such as production downtime, flashing success rate, recurring issues, and software-related first-pass yield​.

  • Turning production issues into sustainable process, tooling, or engineering improvements.



What you bring to the team:

  • Several years of experience in embedded systems, production software, manufacturing test, industrialization, or technical production support​.

  • Experience in serial production or manufacturing environments​.

  • Strong understanding of embedded software, firmware flashing, production diagnostics, and system integration​.

  • Experience with Linux-based embedded systems, ideally NVIDIA Jetson / Orin or similar platforms​.

  • Hands-on experience with scripting, automation, production tooling, and diagnostic workflows​.

  • Ability to analyze complex issues across software, electronics, tooling, process, and operator interaction​.

  • Experience coordinating or leading technical teams​.

  • Strong communication skills across production operators, engineers, quality teams, and management​.

  • A structured, hands-on mindset with the ability to distinguish one-off production issues from systemic process weaknesses​.

  • Ideally, experience in drones, robotics, aerospace, automotive, defense, or industrial electronics​.

  • Ideally, knowledge of CAN, UART, Ethernet, USB, SWD, JTAG, I2C, SPI, MES, ERP, traceability systems, or Operations1.

data.description:

Mitti by SafetyCulture is a global tech company, just not the kind you're picturing. Our almost 1,000-person team builds tools that make work better for the three billion frontline workers who keep the world moving. We've got big tech scale, without the sign-off layers or corporate theatre. This next chapter is about scaling smart, powered by AI, a clear vision and real ownership.

Big tech impact, without the big tech ick.

Role Purpose

This role exists to unlock technical value for Mitti’s customers, designing and implementing solutions that ensure customers integrate deeply with the platform and realise measurable operational outcomes, while bridging the gap between Go-to-Market (GTM) teams and Product, Design & Engineering (PDE). They own end-to-end delivery of integration offerings within defined scope, timeline, and budget, escalating only where customer requirements exceed standard package boundaries.

 

Key Responsibilities

Drive customer success and stickiness

  • Own technical solution design for select customers: from scoping integrations and data workflows through to working implementations that enable full platform value.

  • Deliver the standard Integration/Automation packages end-to-end: scope confirmation, project delivery, build, testing, and handoff within the defined timeline and effort budget.

  • Advise customers and partners on integration architecture: how to connect Mitti to their existing systems effectively and sustainably.

  • Partner with Customer Success Managers (CSMs) to build implementation plans that accelerate time-to-value for managed accounts.

  • Work alongside Account Executives (AEs) during pre-sales to communicate technical platform capabilities (APIs, security architecture, and cloud integrations) and resolve technical blockers in the sales cycle.

  • Act as a technical bridge between GTM and PDE, capturing and routing customer integration feedback that shapes the product roadmap.

  • Partner with the API and Integrations Engineering team to resolve complex customer requirements and advocate for platform improvements that benefit the broader customer base.

data.description:
Who are we?

Smarkets is a prediction market exchange for sports and political trading, having handled over $50 billion in volume since 2010. Security sits within Infrastructure and Engineering, protecting the distributed, real-time systems behind our trading engine. The team's remit spans our core products and our DCM/DCO entities, with a real regulatory dimension to the work, particularly around our CFTC-regulated business units. Alongside that regulatory scope, the focus is squarely on hands-on engineering: designing, building, and shipping the security tooling and controls that let engineering teams move fast safely.

About the Role:

This is a founding build. You'll stand up security engineering from the ground up through go-live and mature it as we scale, working within Infrastructure and Engineering teams to build the controls, automation, and guardrails our trading systems and regulated entities need.

What you will do:

  • Build the Foundations: Be part of a founding build, standing up security engineering from the ground up through go-live and maturing it as we scale, working within Infrastructure and Engineering teams.

  • Design Guardrails: Design, build, and deploy security controls and guardrails across cloud-native platforms, including AI security solutions protecting customer-facing and internal products.

  • Automate as Code: Automate security processes as code, embedding compliance and infrastructure-as-code checks into CI/CD pipelines without slowing down frequent shipping.

  • Assess & Remediate: Conduct risk audits and assessments, translating findings into practical recommendations for engineering teams, and be hands-on in implementing those recommendations.

  • Monitor & Respond: Monitor and analyse system access logs, flag anomalies, and support incident response, containment, and post-incident root cause analysis.

  • Plan for Resilience: Plan and test security backups and disaster recovery processes to keep the platform resilient.

  • Maintain Compliance: Develop and maintain security policies, standards, and controls meeting DCM/DCO requirements, and maintain evidence and documentation to support regulatory examinations and audits.

  • Partner Across Teams: Partner with business and engineering teams on solutions, translating technical work for product and engineering audiences.

  • Champion Ownership: Build a culture of security ownership among engineers, acting as a security partner rather than a gatekeeper.

Role Requirements:

  • Security Engineering Background: Hands-on experience building security engineering/DevSecOps capabilities in a cloud-native, high-growth environment, ideally financial services or exchange infrastructure.

  • Confident Communicator: Comfortable communicating security risk, controls and technical decisions verbally and in writing to external stakeholders such as auditors or regulators.

  • Regulatory Familiarity: Familiarity with CFTC system safeguards expectations, including 17 C.F.R. § 38.1051 and § 39.18 or similar regulatory requirements.

  • AppSec Foundations: Strong grasp of application security principles (OWASP Top 10, NIST) and secure SDLC practices.

  • CI/CD & Tooling: Proficiency with CI/CD tooling (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Azure DevOps, CircleCI) and security tools (Snyk, Aqua, Trivy, Checkov, Twistlock, Clair).

  • Cloud & Container Security: Hands-on expertise securing AWS/Azure/GCP, Kubernetes, containers, and IaC.

  • Compliance as Code: Working knowledge of infrastructure-as-code and compliance-as-code practices.

  • Automation Proficiency: Proficiency in at least one of Python, Bash, or Go, with a track record of automating security processes.

  • Nice-to-have: Demonstrated experience deploying AI security solutions, guardrails, and defences for AI systems used by customers; a personal interest in sports, exchanges, or trading; certifications such as DSOP, CKS, CISSP, CCSP, CSSLP, or an AWS/Azure/GCP Security Specialty; a track record of security automation at scale in Agile/Scrum environments; direct experience with regulators/examiners on technology and system safeguards; and familiarity with event contracts, prediction markets, or similar novel futures products under CFTC.

data.description:
Help Us Build The Future of Travel

At Airalo, we're making it easier for people to stay connected wherever they travel. As the world's first eSIM store, we help millions of travelers access affordable mobile data in 200+ countries and regions around the world.

Today, we're a team of 400+ people across 60+ countries, building a product used by travelers every day. We've grown quickly, but we've worked hard to keep what matters: trust, ownership, and the freedom for people to do great work without unnecessary layers or bureaucracy.

We're fully remote by design, genuinely global, and united by a shared mission to make travel simpler for everyone.

  • Languages: English is our main working language day to day, so you'll need to be comfortable communicating in it both in meetings and async.

 


We're looking for a Staff Data Scientist, Pricing to build the analytical and machine learning capability that pricing runs on, from demand modelling through to the systems that recommend price.

You won't be starting from zero. We've invested in the foundational data and infrastructure that pricing decisions depend on. What's missing is the capability on top: models the business trusts, experiments that settle pricing questions with evidence, and economics defined once so they hold consistently across Commercial, Product and the customer experience.

The arc of the role runs from measurement to prediction to prescription - understanding how demand responds to price, forecasting how it will respond, and ultimately building the models that recommend the price itself.


What You'll Do:

  • Build and own the demand and elasticity modelling capability, quantifying how price affects volume across destination, duration, data tier, and customer segment.

  • Develop machine learning models for demand forecasting and willingness-to-pay, and take them from exploration through to production with the monitoring and retraining that keeps them honest.

  • Move us from predictive to prescriptive by building the optimisation layer that turns forecasts and elasticities into recommended prices under margin, competitive and partner constraints.

  • Design and analyse pricing experiments with statistical rigour, and apply causal methods where clean randomisation isn't possible.

  • Define pricing within our data ecosystem, owning the governed definitions of price, cost and package economics that reporting, analysis and product surfaces all read from.

  • Partner with Commercial and Finance to connect pricing decisions to margin and revenue, and to size opportunities before we commit.

  • Set the analytical standard for pricing at Airalo, from what counts as evidence through to how a model or recommendation gets validated before it influences live pricing.


    • What You'll Bring:

  • 7+ years in data science, quantitative economics, or applied research, including pricing, monetisation, or marketplace economics work that demonstrably changed decisions.

  • Experience with dynamic or algorithmic pricing systems in production.

  • An advanced degree in Econometrics, Statistics, Operations Research or similar, or equivalent applied depth in demand estimation and the identification problems that make naive price-quantity regressions wrong.

  • Hands-on machine learning experience across the full lifecycle, from feature engineering and model selection through to deployment

  • Familiarity with optimisation and decision-science methods that turn predictions into recommended actions, whether through constrained optimisation, bandits, or reinforcement learning approaches.

  • Proven experimentation expertise, having designed and defended experiments with a clear view on decision frameworks and common failure modes.

  • Experience building analytical capability where none existed before, turning raw data and a business question into something a commercial team uses repeatedly.

  • Strong data modelling instincts, thinking in reusable definitions and single sources of truth rather than standalone analyses.

  • The ability to move comfortably between financial, product and operational data and connect the analysis to a financial outcome.

  • Genuine partnership instincts, translating between analytical rigour and commercial reality so that Commercial and Product come to you early rather than after the decision.

  • Fluency in the Python ML stack alongside strong SQL, with the engineering hygiene to hand over code that others can run and maintain.

  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to make a methodological argument to people who won't check your standard errors.

  • A self-starter mindset that thrives in ambiguity and brings structure without waiting for permission.

  • Comfort using AI tools to augment analytical work, with a point of view on where they help and where they don't


    • Nice to have:

  • Experience in marketplace, telecom, travel, or subscription/usage-based businesses.

  • Bayesian or hierarchical modelling for sparse segments and long-tail SKUs.

  • Competitive price response modelling, or working with scraped competitor pricing data.

  • Familiarity with dbt, LightDash, or similar semantic/BI layers.

  • Experience designing semantic or metric layers consumed by both analytics and production systems.

  • Experience working in cross-functional teams spanning commercial, finance and product disciplines.

    • If you are interested in this position, please apply via the link.

We’re looking for a Director, Enterprise IT to build and lead a new function at Airalo. Enterprise IT is responsible for the IT estate our team members use every day and the core business systems that run the company, starting with ERP and expanding to the wider corporate application stack as we scale.

This is a build-and-run role. You’ll lead an established IT Operations team (a lead and a team of four) covering service management, endpoints, networking, identity and SSO. You’ll also be the accountable technical owner of our ERP platform, from implementation into steady state. As more corporate tooling moves into your remit, you’ll recruit and structure an Enterprise Applications team and move us away from every function buying and running its own critical systems. Business functions keep ownership of their processes, data and decisions.

You’ll have real ownership in shaping how systems are configured, governed and supported, and in building the team and operating model that carries us through the next stage of growth.

  • Lead the IT Operations team and its lead: set priorities and service levels, with a clear split between run and build work

  • Act as the accountable owner of the ERP platform, including system configuration, workflow design and ongoing maintenance. If vendor selection is still open when you join, lead its final stages with stakeholders to confirm scope, modules and implementation approach
  • Own the design of core ERP configuration areas such as financial consolidation, budgeting and forecasting, master data, and integration with adjacent systems
  • Manage the ERP implementation partner or systems integrator, holding them to scope, quality, timeline and budget
  • Establish change control, testing and release processes for ERP from day one, and own the post-go-live support model (L1 to L3, vendor SLAs, release cadence)
  • Document system configuration, data flows and integration points so no single person is a dependency
  • Own IT general controls, segregation of duties design and monitoring, and audit evidence for corporate systems, supporting compliance certification and SOX-style financial controls where they apply
  • Own disaster recovery, backup and resilience for corporate systems, and work with Security on access policy, device trust and approved or blocked software
  • Partner with the Data team: Enterprise IT owns platforms, integrations and access controls, while Data keeps reporting, analytics, pipelines and data governance
  • Set the approach to AI tools across corporate functions (tooling, access and safe-use guardrails), with functions owning day-to-day use
  • Build the Enterprise Applications team: define roles, then hire and develop the first leads (2 to 3 additional hires expected over time)

Lab49 was founded in 2002 with a deep pool of business and technology talent and a global reach. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

 

Why we're hiring

Nous runs on small teams with real ownership and barely any middle management. That's a big part of how about 30 of us became one of the UK's fastest-growing startups. It also means the work of joining everything up has been spread across the founders and leads, squeezed in around their day jobs. Plans, OKRs, closing the hires that matter, the big company pushes: everyone does a bit of it and nobody owns it.

Last week showed what happens when someone does. We ran "crunch week": five days where most of the company dropped its normal work to relaunch Nous as a household agent. Twelve workstreams, one owner each, a short daily sync and a pre-mortem. In a week we rebuilt onboarding and the website, shipped new agent capabilities, and got legal, security and comms ready for launch. As one of the team said afterwards, when we cluster around a problem for a bit, we do loads of work.

We want that pace more of the time, without a founder having to drop everything to run it. So we're hiring a Chief of Staff.

 

About the role

You'll work directly with Greg (our CEO) and the founding team, and own how Nous runs day to day: the pace, planning and OKRs, and the big company pushes, plus overseeing hiring and helping land the hires that matter most. You'll sit in the management meeting and get the full picture, including the things that aren't public yet. And you'll have the authority to change how we work: cancel or reshape meetings, and move people and cut scope during a big push.

You enjoy coordinating, but only because it gets things done faster. You'd rather get a decision made today than design a process for making decisions.

 

What you'll actually do

  • Set the pace. Spot what's stuck, work out why, and get it moving. Usually it's a decision nobody has made yet, so you get it made, or make it yourself.

  • Own planning and OKRs. Quarterly OKRs, the weekly management meeting, planning and offsites. Squads run pretty autonomously; you make sure they're working to the same priorities. Each of these should take up less of everyone's time with you running it, not more.

  • Own the scorecard. Keep the numbers behind our OKRs current, and say each week what's off track and why. You pull the data yourself (SQL, our BI tool, a spreadsheet) rather than chasing people for updates.

  • Run the big pushes. The next crunch week is yours: scope it with the leadership team, pick the owners, run it, and write up what we'd do differently next time.

  • Oversee hiring, and help close the hires that matter. Hiring managers run their own processes, and you won't be running ten of them. But you'll keep an eye on all of them, know where every search stands, and jump in where needed. Mostly that's closing the people we really want: working out what they care about and how to win them. Sometimes it's getting a recruiter excited about working with Nous, or unsticking a process that's gone quiet.

  • Represent Nous. You'll talk to recruiters and senior candidates from day one. Over time, and where it helps, you'll represent us to partners, suppliers and investors too.

  • Automate the boring bits. You'd rather build the Monday status digest with Claude than write it by hand every week. Anything you find yourself doing every week is a candidate for automating.

 

What this role isn't

  • An assistant. Diaries and inboxes are someone else's job.

  • A process role. If your first instinct is a new meeting, template or tracker, this probably won't suit you. With you here we should have fewer recurring meetings, not more.

  • A product role. Squads own what gets built, and strategy stays with the founders. You'll be in the room for both, and you make sure nobody's blocked.

  • A recruiter. You oversee hiring and step in where it matters; hiring managers still run their own processes.

  • A dumping ground for jobs nobody else wants. You'll pick up odd jobs, as everyone here does, but the bulk of the role is above.

 

What success looks like

In your first 90 days:

  • The company runs noticeably better: decisions get made faster and fewer things stall. Ask the leads and they'd say so.

  • Something that had been stuck for weeks has shipped because you got involved.

  • You've helped close at least one hire we really wanted.

  • Next quarter's OKRs are set, and the scorecard is current every week.

  • At least one piece of weekly coordination (the OKR update, the status round-up) runs as an AI workflow you built, and nobody does it by hand any more.

  • We have fewer recurring meetings than when you joined.

After a year:

  • You've led two or three company-wide pushes that shipped what they set out to.

  • The senior hires you helped close have said yes and are doing well.

  • Planning, OKRs and the weekly meetings run fine for a month without you.

  • Most of the routine coordination runs on workflows and tools you built, not on meetings.

 

About you

You've got 4–7 years behind you (perhaps a little more if you've switched careers), probably a mix of a fast-growing startup and somewhere that taught you structure: consulting, BizOps or strategy and ops at a scale-up, a founder's office, or product work where you ran launches across teams. Maybe you've founded something.

You coordinate because you're impatient. You notice the thing that's been stuck for a week, and you're the one who unsticks it.

You're persuasive. You can work out what a candidate is really optimising for and how to close them, get a busy recruiter excited about Nous, and hold your own with senior people outside the company.

You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a quick model, write a bit of SQL or find the right dashboard, and tell a real trend from noise.

AI tooling is already how you work. Claude, Claude Code or similar is where you get things done, not something you tried once.

You write clearly and quickly. Most of this job happens in writing: kick-off notes, weekly updates, closing emails.

You tell people the truth, founders included, and you keep confidences. You'll see salaries, plans and people issues before anyone else does.

You listen and you care, but you don't do politics. This role has more connective tissue with others than anyone else in the business, so by playing it straight and being an honest broker, you are also establishing an important norm.

Low ego. Some of the job is unglamorous and you do it anyway.

Bonus points:

  • You've closed hard candidates, or worked in recruiting, talent or BD.

  • You've run a company planning cycle, an offsite or a launch end to end.

  • You've worked somewhere regulated (energy, fintech, insurance).

  • You've automated a chunk of your own job and have something to show for it.

  • You are commercially astute or professionally experienced in a deep domain like law or accounting.

 

How you will grow

This might not be a forever role, and that's fine. You'll see more of how a fast-growing company works than almost anyone else here, which tends to open doors: running a new category as we expand, leading a function, or a commercial or operations role. Or the role grows with the company. Either way, we'll talk about it properly once you've been here a year.

 

Remuneration and benefits

Compelling packages, including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

An environment where you can do your best work:

  • 🏢 A great office set up for lots of collaborative working. We already need more whiteboards

  • 💻 The equipment / setup / training you need to do your best work (and of course, AI subscriptions, including Claude Code Max tier)

  • 🤝 A high-context environment with lots of exposure to the big decisions - be in the room when it happens (literally)

  • 🏡 Flexibility around remote work. If you sometimes just need to get your head down, that's fine

  • ☕ Very good coffee

  • 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house

  • 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots!

  • ✈ 33 days paid holidays (including bank holidays)

  • 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme

  • 🚴 Travel benefits, including the cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans

Nous has an office-first culture. That means we encourage in-person working, and most people do work from the office in Farringdon most of the time. We do a lot of brainstorming, problem-solving and interaction within the team and presence makes this more effective. It also helps ensure people have good peripheral awareness and high context. But we are pragmatic not doctrinal about this, and recognise that, sometimes, certain types of work can be better done remotely. Most team members spend 3-4 days a week in the office on average. This role may naturally involve even more presence than that.

 

The environment

Most importantly, this is a high-performance, high-agency and high-trust technical environment. Nous is intentionally lean and AI-native, not just in its product but as a company. Everyone is expected to use AI to its full potential, whether that's debugging a system, streamlining a workflow or improving how customers are served. Rather than building layers of middle management, we hire smart, high-agency people and give them real ownership.

We're dedicated to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace, and we actively welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds. Every candidate is thoughtfully considered, without regard to race, religion, gender expression, disability or sexual orientation.

If you don't tick every box but think you'd be great at this, get in touch anyway.

data.description:
About Nous

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

 

How we build (worth reading before the role)

How products get built is changing fast. With AI tooling, a PM can prototype, dig into production data and commit production code to get a change live all in an afternoon. An engineer can own a product area end to end and decide what to build next.

We're leaning into that. Our PMs lean into code and our engineers run products: one of our engineers owns the car insurance targets. We care about whatever gets the job done most effectively, regardless of once upon a time whose job it was meant to be.

We're moving fast and adapting as we go, and we don't have all the answers yet. What should a squad look like when everyone can build? Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out.

 

About the role

So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you’d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role.

You’ll take a squad responsible for a key section of our product and service lines and grow them: expand what they cover, understand the levers that drive their performance (automation, new suppliers, what we recommend to members) and increase their commercial value.

Being a Product Manager at Nous is one of the hardest roles we have. The product is complex and we move fast, so you need to be able to hold a lot of context. You'll switch between very different things all day: thinking about OKRs and the plan for the next couple of weeks one moment, getting a PR into production the next, while helping unblock an engineer.

That's also what makes it exciting.

You bring order to fast-moving work, get some sequencing in place so people aren’t each figuring it out on their own, evaluate what’s being shipped, own the reporting and keep the squad’s energy up. You won’t hesitate to make changes yourself, but you won’t be just another builder in the squad either: when you’re heads-down building, you can’t unblock anyone or bring the team together.

Growing a service line here means working across the boundary between product and commercial, so we’re particularly interested in PMs who’ve had real exposure to the commercial side of a business.

Our agent acts in the real world a lot, so saving someone money takes more than great product execution. We also need access to the best tariffs and suppliers, and we have to understand the regulation we operate in. And because Nous is an agent, your nice neat Amplitude funnels don't work: every user's journey can be totally different. So we're after PMs who are excited by everything it takes to make an agentic product work for real households, including the bits that wouldn't traditionally count as "product".

Worth being upfront: we can't tell you yet which service lines you'd own. It depends on the Venn diagram of your particular skill set and the problems we need to solve at the point you join.

 

What matters most

We need all of these at once:

  • Sharp. You pick things up quickly and enjoy hard problems. Given a messy one, you can lay out what you know and what you'd check first, then change your mind as new data turns up.

  • Adaptable. We’re working a lot of this out as we go, so the role and the squad will change, probably more than once. You enjoy that. You pick up whatever’s needed, PM work or not, and you work in the open: sharing rough thinking early and changing course when someone has a better idea.

  • Delivery. You bring order to a fast-moving squad: clear priorities, sensible sequencing, people unblocked quickly, and an honest look at whether what shipped actually worked.

  • Product craft. You find the real problem behind a request and make the trade-offs explicit. You care about the details of what our users actually see.

  • Commercial and analytical. You know what your area made last month, what moved it and what you'd do next, and you answer most of your own questions with data. You think in conversion, margin and lifetime value as readily as in features.

  • Energy. You've probably worked at a startup. You move fast, you're happy doing the unglamorous work yourself, and you'd rather ship this week's version than polish next quarter's.

And everyone builds here, PMs included. You'll use AI tooling (Claude Code or whatever gets it done) to prototype, dig into data and ship changes yourself. You don't need to be an engineer, but you shouldn't be scared of code.

 

What you'll actually do

  • Grow your service lines. Understand what really drives their performance, be able to measure it, and lead the squad to deliver it.

  • Set the squad's OKRs and roadmap, get the sequencing in place, and drive fast, efficient execution.

  • Evaluate what’s being shipped, and own the reporting: make sure the reports and the data behind them make sense.

  • Work across product and commercial: the suppliers and tariffs we can offer, the regulation we work within, and what that means for what gets built.

  • Run experiments, and unblock yourself on the analysis without always needing an analyst.

  • Get close to members and ops. Read the conversations, sit with the people handling the edge cases, and fix the parts of the journey where people drop out or get stuck.

 

About you

You'll likely thrive here if:

  • You've been a PM for a few years, ideally at a startup, and you've owned something with a number attached: revenue, conversion, retention.

  • You've worked on the commercial side as well as the product side: a P&L, a supplier or partner relationship, pricing, or a whole service line.

  • You're comfortable enough with data and code to unblock yourself.

Nice-to-haves:

  • You were a software engineer before you moved into product.

  • You've worked on a transactional or regulated product: insurance, fintech, energy, marketplaces.

  • You've built and shipped your own thing: a startup, a side project, an internal tool that took off.

This probably isn't for you if your PM experience is mostly roadmaps and stakeholder management at a big company, with no number you owned.

 

How we work

We keep the middle thin, on purpose. There's barely any middle management, which means fewer bottlenecks and room for exceptional people to have real impact without first being promoted into managing others. It's a real bet, not a free lunch. Instead of a manager buffer, you get lots of context and colleagues who help because they're invested, not because an org chart says so. If you need a clear remit handed down before you can move, this probably won't suit you.

Your first 90 days are built around getting you to real ownership safely: pairing when you want it, lots of context, and people who want you to ship. We celebrate the person who built the unglamorous version this week, not whoever thought of it first.

We're office-first, near Farringdon. We do a lot of our best thinking together and being in the same room helps, though we're pragmatic about heads-down work when you need it.

 

Remuneration and benefits

Compelling package including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough to pay real salaries, and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

  • 🏢 A great office set up for collaborative work (we already need more whiteboards)

GTM Associate

London, 4x days per week in-office

Vega is looking for A-players to help build the commercial engine and take on a revenue-driving seat. You will be a clients’ very first touchpoint with Vega; running outbound, supporting growth and marketing initiatives, and building systems that support hyper-growth.

About Vega

Vega is transforming the way private markets operate. Alternative asset management is one of the most influential forces in the global economy, with over $20TN in assets today. Over the next five years, the industry is set to grow 3x, but GPs are facing challenges around their ability to handle the investment flows that are coming in. GPs have been completely underserved by innovation, particularly on the investor relations side.

Vega built the industry’s first AI-native operating system, where all client work gets done - from the start of an investor’s journey to its end. We are rethinking how work gets done in private markets from first principles: the opportunity is big, but it’s also niche, high-stakes, and difficult to get right.

Who we are

We are still at the beginning of our journey. Vega was founded by former investors at Elliott and KKR, and built by talent from the world’s leading technology and financial services firms - including Trade Republic, Revolut, Goldman Sachs, BCG, and more. We have raised $30M so far, with the backing of Apollo, Motive Partners, and 60+ senior executives from the industry. Today, we have over $300B AUM and 30,000 users on the platform, and we have much more left to do.

How we do it

Vega is a fast-growing startup. We want to make this a career-accelerating place for people with the ambition to build something big. If the below sounds appealing, it could be for you:

  1. We do not seek consensus. You will be expected to voice opinions and take initiative. Vega's best people do not wait to be told what to do before finding solutions to problems they have spotted.

  2. We believe bureaucracy is the killer of progress. We are focused on creating the minimum viable process to operate with quality at speed.

  3. We prioritise talent over tenure. There is no promise of progression without performance – we assess and reward people on impact above all else.

Read up on our $100m Series C

Missions

As Alan’s Corporate Paralegal, you will own the corporate governance of a fast-growing international group (six jurisdictions and a dozen entities today, more in the coming months) and rebuild how that work gets done with AI. The role has three parts:

Own Alan’s corporate governance with full ownership.

  • Prepare Boards, General Meetings and committees documentation across the group, with internal teams and auditors;

  • Keep entity records, registers and filings accurate and up to date;

  • Run the annual accounts approval and filings for each entity, with Finance and auditors;

  • Be the go-to contact for shareholder and Board questions;

  • Support cross-border projects with research and drafting.

Build the governance playbook as Alan expands.

  • Set up governance for each new entity, in a way the next one can reuse;

  • Write the playbooks, templates and guidance local teams need to follow our processes;

  • Adapt equity frameworks and documentation to new countries and local rules.

Automate the repetitive work with AI.

  • Build workflows that run in the background with light human review, using no-code tools and Alan’s internal AI, with support from our tooling team;

  • Start with recurring events such as meeting minutes, equity movements and the filings calendar.

You will join the Corporate Governance Area, led by Anne-Lise Delfanne, and work alongside a team of legal and corporate operations experts. Our collaboration model encourages growth and curiosity, so you will never feel cornered in your role.

Key outcomes after six months

After six months, you will have:

  • Taken ownership of the recurring governance work for our French entities;

  • Built AI agents and workflows that take a large share of manual work off you and the team;

  • Improved our templates and documentation;

  • Reviewed or drafted legal documents in several areas;

  • Supported our international expansion, for example by opening an entity or onboarding a local team on our processes;

  • Built strong working relationships with the Corporate Governance Area, Finance, People and local advisors.

From then onwards, the role grows with you: M&A, fundraising, reorganisations and more.

Profile and competencies

Skills

This role sits at the intersection of legal knowledge, corporate operations, and AI tooling. We don't expect anyone to arrive fully skilled across all three dimensions. What matters most is your ownership mindset and genuine appetite to build. For the rest, we'll grow together.

  • Experience: Ideally 2+ years owning corporate secretarial work, as a paralegal in a law firm, in legal or corporate ops in-house, or as a company secretary.

  • Legal knowledge: a law degree or paralegal qualification, and/or hands-on experience with several of the following: board and shareholder documentation, entity management, corporate filings, equity documentation, due diligence or transaction coordination;

  • (Bonus) AI and tooling appetite: you already use no-code or AI tools (e.g. Make, Zapier, Notion automations) to save time, or you are keen to learn fast;

  • Language: excellent written and spoken English (working language at Alan) and French.

We encourage applications from career changers who do not have all the above qualifications, if you have a strong interest in working at the heart of corporate operations and willingness to learn fast.

  • Highly organised and rigorous, with exceptional attention to detail;

⭐ The Product Marketing Manager B2C opportunity

Building the engagement engine with Alan Play that makes 500k members come back to their health every single day, a key differentiator for Alan.

 

Today, 25k Alan members open Alan Play every day (120,000 every month) to walk, meditate, breathe, compete with their colleagues, build healthy habits. Play is Alan's #1 source of traffic and the retention engine of all our health services. And we are B2B2C: companies pay, members choose to engage. Play is a differentiator in deals, and at renewal. HR admins are also an underused distribution channel to reach members. Two audiences, one product story. By 2030 we want 500k daily users, across all our countries

 

The challenges: Our lifecycle is greenfield. Onboarding, activation, reminders, reactivation and win-back are owned by nobody today. We run events rebuilt almost from scratch, so the tenth Alan Cup costs as much as the first. We measure opens and clicks, not what a campaign actually did to daily engagement. And on the B2B side, our pitch goes stale between releases, as Play ships fast, so the sales argument does not keep up.

 

The future: A lifecycle layer designed for personalisation, running on the segmentation and experimentation platform Play has been building. Campaign machinery that gets cheaper every quarter. A measurement loop we trust, with holdouts and real incrementality. A live Play pitch that updates as features ship, so the field walks into a renewal or a deal with the current product. And HR admins turned into a real, measured distribution channel rather than a mailing list.

 

The hard parts: This role is horizontal, and vertical. Many member segments, many admin segments, several countries, coordination with Product as well as Sales, KAM and CSM, as well as other products teams who communicate with members.

 

⭐ Is it you we’re looking for?

 

Must haves

  • Retention and lifecycle marketing at scale on a consumer product - subscription, gaming, social, media, health and fitness. Where engagement and retention are the business.

  • You build systems, not just campaigns - you can walk us through machinery you built that made the next campaign cheaper, and tell us what it cost you to get it adopted.

  • Analytical rigour - you read a funnel, design a segment, set up a holdout, call a result. You are comfortable being accountable to a product metric.

  • Horizontal operator - you have held many audiences and several countries at once. Volume and context switching, not depth on a single vertical.

  • Genuinely hands on - you want to run the campaigns yourself at the start. This is the ramp up, and the condition for standardising well afterwards.

  • Branding sensitivity : you can express the personality of the product you market and create great moments

  • You write well and fast. Emotion generating copy and branding is a real part of the job

  • Marketing automation at scale - Customer.io, Braze, Iterable or equivalent.

  • Missionary mindset and a real attachment to the health mission.

  • B2B2C sensibility: you can maintain weigh in both segments

 

Nice to haves

  • French, Spanish or Dutch on top of English, for four-country localisation

  • HR tech, employee benefits or workplace wellbeing

  • Gamification, challenges or social mechanics

  • Experience standardising something that other teams then reused

 

Not a fit if

  • You describe success in open and click rates

  • You only want to talk to members, and see commercial side as somebody else's job

  • You need a brief, or someone who writes the strategy for you

  • You want to delegate execution from day one

  • You treat positioning as PMM-only territory, or platform teams as a service desk

  • You are uncomfortable with ambiguity, or need a big team to be effective

  • Flexible vacation policy and flexible working hours. Organize your time as you wish.

  • Transport. Country-specific commuter benefits.

  • Learning & Training opportunities. A highly flexible Training policy free books and budget to attend and speak at conferences if the opportunity arises.

  • Personal growth through coaching: At Alan, coaching isn't just a perk - it's core to who we are. At its core, Alan is a tech company that believes exceptional member experience is a competitive advantage: fast, empathetic, and reliable service at scale. As of Q1 2026, 40% of conversations are handled automatically.

  • At the intersection of Care, Legal, Security, and Data Protection sits a set of topics that are as operationally complex as they are strategically critical: data breaches, GDPR rights requests, security incidents, legal complaints, regulatory reporting.

  • We are looking for a Care Legal & Security Specialist to own these topics end-to-end: handling complex cases in close collaboration with Alan's Legal and DPO teams, building the processes and training that allow our ~300 Care agents to manage them with confidence, and identifying where AI and automation can reduce manual load. As Alan accelerates across four countries, what you build in France gets replicated in Spain, Belgium, and Canada: your work doesn't stay local.

  • This is not a pure legal role, and it is not a pure ops role. You handle regulatory cases, improve the processes that prevent them from recurring, and scale what works across countries. You will be embedded within our Operational Excellence team, working in close collaboration with Care Ops and the Corporate Unit.

    👨‍🚀 Missions

    1/ Operational run (60%)

  • Handle complex security incidents, GDPR cases, and legal complaints escalated from Care agents, including CNIL notifications (drafted in close collaboration with Legal and DPO, within the 72-hour regulatory deadline), account takeover situations, Level 2 and Level 3 complaints, and incoming legal mail

  • Manage interactions with external stakeholders (CNIL, Insurance Ombudsman, Signal Conso) with precision and within regulatory deadlines

  • Own KPI monitoring and reporting for legal and security matters; organize yearly complaints reporting for Alan's Board; identify trends and escalate systemic issues to Product teams early

    2/ Scalability: process, tools, and training (20%)

  • Design and continuously improve workflows, escalation paths, macros, and help center content so Care agents can handle legal and security cases autonomously at L1 and L2

  • Identify simplification and automation opportunities across legal and security operations, then collaborate with Care Ops and Product crews to deploy them, rather than solving each case manually

  • Build and maintain training materials (case studies, Q&As, simulations), so Care Experts develop real judgment, not just process familiarity

  • Ensure regulatory training completion across the team

    3/ Globalization (20%)

  • Translate processes, frameworks, and training materials built for France into resources that Care and Legal/Compliance teams in other countries can adopt

  • Coordinate actively with counterparts in other countries to share learnings, align on best practices, and anticipate regulatory divergences

  • Build shared resources so that when a new country goes live, the Care Legal & Security function isn't starting from scratch

To deliver on those missions, you will:

  • Support Care Experts participating in the Legal & Security taskforce: build their judgment on complex and ambiguous cases, be the primary escalation reference for Care agents facing difficult legal or security situations

  • Collaborate with the Corporate Unit Lead and Care Ops to shape the Care roadmap on legal and security topics; translate regulatory constraints into executable processes and surface operational insights that should inform policy or product decisions

    ⭐ You'll excel in this role if you:

  • Deliver reliably on high-stakes, deadline-driven cases with a real member-centric mindset

  • Have at least 1-2 years of experience in one of the following: GDPR / privacy operations, legal complaints handling in a regulated sector, or compliance ops in fintech, insurtech, or health

  • Communicate with precision and adapt to your audience, whether you're briefing a legal expert, aligning with a product team, or coaching a front-line agent. You get buy-in from agents and managers who didn't ask for a new process, and that's as important as designing the process itself

  • Spot simplification opportunities and know how to turn them into projects: you identify what should be automated or redesigned, then drive the collaboration with Care Ops and Product to make it happen

  • Are comfortable navigating regulatory frameworks (GDPR, complaint handling, CNIL) without being a lawyer; you know when to escalate and when to own it, and you're backed by Legal and DPO experts at Alan

  • Are comfortable making judgment calls in ambiguous situations and moving forward without waiting for all the answers.

  • Are fluent in French (C1+ written and spoken, essential for CNIL notifications, ombudsman responses, and legal correspondence) and proficient in English for internal Alan collaboration

En collaboration directe avec les managers des différentes équipes, tu seras chargé.e de comprendre leurs besoins et de les aider à recruter les personnes les plus adaptées. Il s'agit d'un poste central chez Doctrine, et tu contribueras directement à notre croissance.
Tu feras partie de l'équipe People et sera rattaché.e à notre DRH, Gabrielle de Luppé, et en plus des hiring managers, tu travailleras au quotidien avec quatre autres TAM qui connaissent parfaitement Doctrine.
Nous te proposons de développer ta connaissance des métiers d'une entreprise tech, et de construire progressivement ton autonomie sur toutes les étapes du recrutement, du sourcing au closing.

  • Mener en autonomie des entretiens, à distance comme en présentiel
  • Être un partenaire des candidats, en t’assurant que leur expérience soit la plus agréable et efficace possible
  • Être un partenaire des managers, en échangeant régulièrement avec eux sur les différents candidats et sur leurs besoins
  • Proposer et mettre en œuvre des améliorations aux process de recrutement de Doctrine
  • Proposer et contribuer aux initiatives marque employeur (salons, communication, partage d'expérience, qualité...)

    • Profil
  • Tu as une expérience confirmée en recrutement dans un environnement startup / scale up.
  • Tu as un excellent relationnel, tu sais établir facilement un contact humain de qualité
  • Tu es réputé pour être un véritable business partner pour les hiring managers
  • Tu arrives à avoir une approche data-oriented et à piloter ton activité recrutement à travers la data
  • L'approche directe n'a pas de secret pour toi
  • Tu parles anglais couramment et la maitrise de l'espagnol est un plus ! 

    • Ce qui t'attend si tu rejoins Doctrine 🤝

    • Contribuer à un projet ambitieux, avec un impact réel et positif sur la société : rendre le droit plus accessible et plus ouvert.
    • Un onboarding très complet permettant une intégration et une montée en compétence rapides.
    • Une aventure dans laquelle la formation et le partage des connaissances font partis du quotidien.

data.title: Experienced/Senior Machine Learning Engineer - Squad Distribute
data.description:
Our Mission ⚖️

At Doctrine, we're building Europe's leading legal AI platform.

Our belief? Law shouldn't be slowed down by repetitive tasks. It should be augmented by a specialised AI, designed to understand, analyse and produce legal reasoning at the highest standard.

Our ambition? To help legal professionals work with greater reliability, efficiency and peace of mind, through a single, comprehensive and secure platform.

Today, 27,000 legal professionals across five countries (France, Italy, Germany, Spain and Luxembourg) trust us to do just that.

Our growth is guided by a clear approach: a global vision, grounded in a deep understanding of local specificities.

Behind this ambition, a team of around 250 people, united around one goal: supporting lawyers and legal professionals at every stage of their work, from research to drafting.

And we're just getting started.


Context

We are looking for a confirmed/senior Machine Learning Engineer to help us build the first legal AI platform.

Join a squad dedicated to revolutionizing how legal professionals advise clients and businesses across France and Europe. A high-impact product squad responsible for secondary legal sources and private documents. These are complex challenges where you will also contribute to embedding GenAI at the core of our products. 

You can find full details about our stack on GitHub https://github.com/DoctrineLegal/#our-tech-stack !
 
Note: Previous professional experience in law is not required, but a willingness to learn and develop expertise in understanding legal documents is important 🙂

Missions 🛠
  • Develop NLP models (whether based on Machine Learning or not) to assist with information search and recommendation within legal documents, in particular.
  • Maintain and monitor these models in production.
  • Design conversational agents to accelerate lawyers’ work across various areas of law, ensuring accurate responses and facilitating drafting tasks.
  • Collaborate with different types of profiles, including engineers, product managers, and product designers, to identify new product development opportunities.
  • Participate in internal knowledge sharing and consolidation of best practices; contribute to the development of our Engineering strategy.

    • Ideal Profile 👀
  • Strong knowledge of Machine Learning (both classical and deep learning) for data extraction and recommendation, ideally with some first-hand experience with LLMs.
  • Experience with natural language search engines and inverted indexes such as Elasticsearch.
  • Solid understanding of MLOps challenges, with a strong motivation to grow in this area.
  • A keen interest in artificial intelligence topics.
  • Desire to identify, analyze, and deploy the latest scientific advances in production.
  • Strong Python development skills, with a focus on algorithm design.
  • Proficiency in French, as you will be working with legal data in French.

    • Extras of the role 👁
  • Like all engineers at Doctrine, you will join one of our cross-functional chapters — in this case, the Web chapter. Within this chapter, you will contribute to internal projects aimed at improving our processes and shaping our long-term vision. The chapter meets every week to:
  • Share knowledge: keep track of the state of the art, review scientific papers, continuous improvement, best practices, etc.
  • Propose improvements: experiment with new tools, suggest new processes to implement.
  • You will also take part in recruitment: all individual contributors meet candidates through technical assessments or interviews.

    • What's in it for you ☀️

    🏡 A flexible remote work policy, allowing up to three days of remote work per week (depending on your team).

    🌴 A flexible leave policy

    🌱 Real internal mobility opportunities

    🏄‍♂️ Regular team events

    📚 A genuine focus on individual and collective learning, with a €750 annual budget for any training related to your role, plus team-wide and company-wide training sessions

    🏋️‍♀️ A Gymlib subscription for sports and wellness activities

    🧘 Free access to the Moka.care mental health support platform, including up to 6 individual sessions per year

    👩‍⚕️ Health insurance with Alan

    🍱🚲 A Swile card for meal vouchers and sustainable mobility allowance (€66.60/month)

    💡 Discounts and perks via our Works Council (CSE) on the Happypal platform

    🍏 Brand new Apple equipment

    Our values 🤝

    At Doctrine, our 4 values guide us every day as we work to move things forward.

    Challenge the status quo: we champion bold ideas that drive change across an entire industry.

    Liberty and responsibility: we encourage autonomy, individual impact and ownership.

    Knowledge is power: information is at the heart of Doctrine's mission, and we constantly strive to grow.

    Release early, release often and listen to your customers: we believe in the power of iteration and in constantly listening to our market, our customers and their challenges.

     Our hiring process 🚀

    1. A 30-min intro call with one of our Talent Acquisition Managers to understand your career goals and walk you through what we're building at Doctrine.
    2. A 1-hour conversation with your future manager to dive into the role, team scope and answer all your questions.
    3. One or two technical assessments to evaluate your skills in practice.
    4. An office visit including: lunch with 3 people from different teams to give you a feel for your future colleagues; a values conversation to share our vision; and a meeting with our CEO, Guillaume.

    (The process can be adapted to fit your personal and professional constraints if needed.)

    Ladies, go ahead and apply!

    Research shows that women in particular tend not to apply for a role when they don't meet every single requirement. To put your mind at ease: this job description is a guide, nothing more.

    If Doctrine interests you, we'd love to hear from you!

    Diversity & inclusion

    All our roles are open to people with disabilities. Feel free to bring it up at any point during the process. We're committed to putting in place whatever adjustments are needed to ensure a working environment that works for everyone.

Le contexte

Nous cherchons plusieurs Account Executives (AE) Mid & Up Market pour rejoindre les équipes qui couvrent le segment Up market corporates :

  • Les ETI et Grandes Entreprises (SBF 120)

Notre équipe commerciale est organisée comme beaucoup de SaaS B2B, avec des BDR qui s'occupent de la relation commerciale avant-vente et qui portent une part de la qualification et de la prospection, des AE qui participent à la prospection et s'occupent principalement de tout le cycle de vente à partir du 1er RDV jusqu’à la finalisation d’un contrat (définition du périmètre, des options, négociation tarifaire).

Pourquoi être AE Mid & Up Market chez Doctrine ?

  • Vendre la Legal Tech la plus performante du marché, qui innove en permanence et est en avance de phase sur les sujets d'IA Générative ;
  • S’appuyer sur des équipes Ops et Marketing bien staffées et de haut niveau, au service de la performance des Sales au quotidien ;
  • Pouvoir évoluer dans une équipe avec des profils divers, qui met l'accent sur la formation et l’accompagnement dès le premier jour ;
  • Bénéficier d'un package attractif comprenant un variable déplafonné.

Les missions 🛠

  • Tu es amené.e à porter le cycle de vente de A à Z : dans une démarche d'acquisition, tu prospectes sur le parc qui t’es confié, qualifies le besoin des comptes, montres la valeur de l’outil au travers de démonstrations, construis des offre financières adaptées, négocies & signes un maximum de deals.
  • Tu adresses principalement ces comptes en outbound, avec un approche multi-interlocuteurs ; tu optimises la vélocité commerciale en équilibrant vitesse d’exécution et taux de transformation.
  • Tu travailles main dans la main avec l’équipe étendue de Doctrine pour générer des opportunités business : tu te coordonnes au quotidien avec les BDR et les CSM/AM qui contribueront directement à ton activité, et tu pourras t’appuyer sur les équipes Ops, Marketing et Product pour accélérer la croissance sur ton segment.

Le profil idéal 👀
